inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 197.8m shares issued and outstanding at 26 Sep 2026 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q balance sheet) plus 5.2m dilutive securities from the Q1 FY2027 EPS note; held FLAT because SBC and equity-award withholding taxes are fully expensed in the flows
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K share-based compensation note ($107.4m expense; $104.5m cash-flow add-back) plus $81.6m taxes paid on net-share settlement (financing activities). Tapestry publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. Withholding taxes run high because the share price roughly tripled across the vesting window; Q1 FY2027 alone was $104m.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Saturday closest to 30 June (FY2026 ended 27 June 2026; FY2027 is a 53-week year ending 3 July 2027)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year UST), equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.3 for a fashion/accessories name with a history of deep brand cycles -> cost of equity ~10.8%. Debt is ~6% of enterprise value at ~5% pre-tax, so WACC ~9.5%. The same 9.5% is used in all three scenarios: brand-cycle risk is charged through the scenario paths and weights, not through a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: straight-line lease cost ($378m fixed + $232m variable in FY2026) sits inside SG&A and therefore inside EBITDA. Operating lease liabilities ($1,672m at 26 Sep 2026) are NOT in net debt. One treatment, lease cost in the flows.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (US consumer-brand operating company; dcf-methods routing row 1). Fresh build, no prior valuation. CONTINUING OPERATIONS BASE: Stuart Weitzman was sold on 4 Aug 2025; base_revenue is FY2026 net sales of $8,004.2m less the $14.6m of Stuart Weitzman stub sales = $7,989.6m (Coach $6,914.7m + Kate Spade $1,074.9m). Margins are anchored to FY2026 non-GAAP operating income of $1,865.8m, which excludes the $98.3m IEEPA tariff-refund credit and $49.7m of divestiture / efficiency / distribution charges: adjusted EBITDA before SBC = 1,865.8 + 217.2 (D&A 160.8 + cloud-computing amortisation 56.4) + 104.5 SBC = ~$2,188m, 27.4% of sales. Capex path includes cloud-computing implementation costs (FY2026 total $217.1m; FY2027 guided ~$300m) to match the amortisation added back. reported_fcf = OCF 1,978.5 - purchases of PP&E 166.0; it includes the divested brand's immaterial stub and a favourable working-capital year (payables +131.6, other liabilities +75.8) partly offset by the $115m tariff-refund receivable, and cash tax paid was only $200.7m (10.8% of pre-tax) against an 18.2% adjusted effective rate, so the FY2026 20% owner-FCF margin is not carried forward: year-1 is built from components at ~18%. Net debt = current debt 597 + long-term debt 1,960 (carrying) less cash 599 and short-term investments 183. Interest income is not stripped because the company is in net debt. Buybacks: $1,554.6m in FY2026 and $603m in Q1 FY2027 ($1.29bn left on the $3.0bn programme) - the flat count is funded many times over; repurchases above the SBC charge are treated as value-neutral. Not in the bridge: the remaining IEEPA refund receivable (under $115m, partly collected in Q1 FY2027; under $0.50/share). Company FY2027 guidance is issued in the earnings press release, which is not in the Extracted folder; the year-1 path is anchored to the Q1 FY2027 10-Q instead (sales +12.0% ex Stuart Weitzman and FX, Coach +16%, Kate Spade -10%; adjusted operating margin 23.2% vs 20.8%). TPR_Analysis.json was not yet available when this was built; narratives draw on the filings.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unusable: book equity fell from $3.26bn (FY2021) to $0.69bn (FY2026) because of ~$5.6bn of buybacks and the FY2025 $855m Kate Spade impairment, not because of losses. It diverges from revenue and EPS CAGRs by far more than 30pp, so revenue 5-year CAGR is used as the anchor instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award withholding taxes): FY2021 1,125.3, FY2023 656.6, FY2026 1,623.5. Owner-FCF 5-year CAGR (7.6%) is slightly below reported (8.5%) because withholding taxes rose from $7.5m to $81.6m. The 3-year figures are flattered by a weak FY2023 base. Historical series include Stuart Weitzman (3-5% of sales, roughly break-even), so they understate continuing-operations growth slightly. EPS CAGRs use GAAP diluted EPS; FY2026 includes the tariff-refund credit.

base.rationale: Year 1 at +8% against a Q1 of +12% ex-divestiture, because comparisons toughen (FY2026 quarters grew 14-21% before slowing to +9% in Q4). EBITDA margin (before SBC, after lease cost) steps up ~80bp in FY2027 on Q1's +240bp adjusted operating-margin gain, then drifts back to 27.5% as tariff relief is lapped and Coach's 36% segment margin normalises a little. SBC path starts at 2.6% because Q1 FY2027 withholding taxes ($104m) already exceed all of FY2026, then glides to 2.0%. Cash tax ramps from the FY2026 cash-paid level toward a Pillar-Two-era 20%. Working capital is a small use of cash on growth (inventory-carrying retailer).

scenario_narratives.base: Coach's momentum moderates rather than breaks. The brand grew 23.5% in FY2026 (North America +23%, Greater China +40%) on younger-customer acquisition and full-price handbag AUR gains, and is still growing mid-teens in Q1 FY2027; the base case lets that decelerate to mid-single digits by FY2029 and to GDP-like growth after. Kate Spade (13% of sales, loss-making, -10% in Q1) stops shrinking by FY2028 but contributes little profit. Margins hold near today's record level - gross margin above 76% and a Coach segment margin in the mid-30s - with a small give-back as Section 301 tariffs replace the refunded IEEPA duties and brand investment continues. Ten-year sales reach ~$12.0bn at a ~17% owner-FCF margin.
scenario_narratives.bull: Coach proves to be a durable compounding franchise rather than a fashion cycle: Gen-Z customer acquisition converts to repeat purchase, Greater China and Europe sustain double-digit growth from a low share base, and footwear and small leather goods broaden the brand beyond the Tabby family. Kate Spade's reset works and it returns to low-teens segment margins, removing a ~$150m drag relative to FY2024. Fixed-cost leverage and continued AUR gains lift EBITDA margin to 30%. This needs both the Coach heat to persist for several more years and the Kate Spade turnaround to land.
scenario_narratives.bear: The fashion cycle turns, as it did for Coach in FY2014-FY2016 when sales fell 17% from peak and operating margin went from 31% to the high teens. The hero-product heat fades, the young cohort moves on, and promotional activity returns to the outlet channel that still carries most North American volume; Greater China gives back part of a 40% growth year. New Section 301 tariffs of 10-12.5% on Asian sourcing are not fully priced through, and Kate Spade keeps shrinking and needs further restructuring. Sales fall ~8% over FY2028-FY2029 and EBITDA margin settles around 22%, close to the FY2019-FY2023 average, with no recovery to the FY2026 peak. Owner FCF stays positive throughout - this is a de-rating and earnings reset, not a solvency case; net debt is under 1x EBITDA.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: margins and growth are at an all-time peak for a fashion business whose lead brand has been through one deep reversal within the last decade, and Kate Spade is still loss-making. Base stays at 50%: moderation from a strong position is the most likely path given 87% DTC mix and a clean balance sheet. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things - multi-year persistence of Coach's heat and a Kate Spade turnaround that has not yet shown up in the numbers.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Tapestry is valued as a two-brand continuing business (Coach ~87% of sales and all of the profit; Kate Spade ~13% and loss-making) on a strict owner-FCF basis: SBC and the cash taxes paid on net-share settlement are both expensed and the diluted share count is held flat. The central question is whether FY2026's record 23% adjusted operating margin and mid-teens growth are a new plateau or a cyclical peak; the scenarios bracket that question directly, and the terminal multiple is capped at 15x owner FCF (12x bear, 17x bull) to reflect fashion-cycle risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: Brand-cycle reversal at Coach: the model's value is almost entirely one brand, and its FY2014-FY2016 history shows how quickly sales and margins can reset

Tariff regime: IEEPA duties were refunded but Section 301 tariffs of 10-12.5% took effect in July 2026 and the Section 122 appeal is unresolved; the base case assumes these are largely offset by pricing and sourcing
Kate Spade: a further impairment or restructuring would not change cash flows much but signals the brand's losses could widen
Equity-award withholding taxes are running well above the SBC expense because of the share-price rise; if they stay near the Q1 FY2027 pace the 2.0% long-run SBC charge is too low
Cash tax rate: FY2026 cash taxes were ~11% of pre-tax income against an 18% book rate; the model ramps to 20% under Pillar Two
FY2027 company guidance was not available in the filings set; year-1 drivers rest on the Q1 FY2027 10-Q run-rate
Greater China is ~17% of sales after a 40% growth year and is the most volatile region
